questions.question_text: A 58-year-old man presented to the accident and emergency department with clinical features suggestive of an occlusion of the right medial striate branch of the anterior cerebral artery. Which of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The medial striate artery, also known as the recurrent artery of Heubner, is the largest perforating   branch of the anterior cerebral artery. An occlusion in the unilateral medial striate artery gives rise   to contralateral paresis of the face and arm, dysarthria and hemichorea. An occlusion of the bilateral   medial striate artery results in akinetic mutism. Ideomotor apraxia is caused by an occlusion in the   pericallosal branch of the anterior cerebral artery. Apathy with some memory loss is caused by an   occlusion in the orbitofrontal polar branch of the anterior cerebral artery occlusion. Tactile anomia   is an inability to recognise an object when presented by touch in the absence of aphasic anomia.   It can occur due to a lesion in the corpus callosum resulting in a disconnection between the tactile   and language areas of the brain.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely neurological damage caused by the lacunar infarct of the genu of the internal capsule?
questions.explanation: The internal capsule is divided into three components such as the anterior limb, genu and posterior   limb. There are five classical lacunar syndromes described in the literature with characteristics signs.   Lacunar infarct in the genu of internal capsules gives rise to dysarthria, clumsiness of one hand   with or without central facial paralysis, dysphasia and tongue deviation, also known as dysarthria  clumsy hand syndrome. Pure motor stroke is the commonest type of lacunar infarct. It occurs due to   an infarct in the posterior limb of the internal capsule and presents with contralateral hemiparesis,   facial weakness with or without dysarthria, and bilateral pure motor stroke. Lacunar infarcts in the   ventral posterior nucleus of the thalamus give rise to a pure sensory syndrome with or without   sensory ataxia. Lacunar infarcts in either the anterior or the posterior internal capsule can also lead   to sensorimotor stroke or ataxic hemiparesis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following functions is most likely to be affected by a lesion in the non-dominant hemisphere?
questions.explanation: Agnosis is an abnormality in the perception of sensation despite a normal sensory pathway.   Anosognosia, which is unawareness of weakness of the affected side, is associated with a   non-dominant parietal lobe lesion. Non-dominant parietal and occipital lesions are linked with   visual and body perception. Other options mentioned in the question occur because of a lesion in   the dominant hemisphere

questions.question_text: Which part of the brain is related to alterations in memory?
questions.explanation: Lesions in the temporal lobe, particularly the middle and inferior temporal gyri, are associated with memory alterations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following lobe lesions is associated with difficulties in calculation, and perceptual and spatial orientation?
questions.explanation: A lesion in the non-dominant parietal lobe can cause difficulties in calculation and spatial orientation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a part of the limbic lobe nuclei?
questions.explanation: The limbic lobe is an arrangement of cortical structures around the diencephalon. It consists of   cortical areas and nuclei. The cortical areas include cingulate gyrus, parahippocampal gyrus and   subcallosal gyrus, whereas nuclei include the amygdaloid nucleus and septal nucleus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a part of the basal ganglia?
questions.explanation: The corpus striatum is a major component of the basal ganglia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cranial nerves innervate intrinsic muscles of larynx?
questions.explanation: The vagus nerve innervates the intrinsic muscles of the larynx.

questions.question_text: Where is the entire nervous system derived from?
questions.explanation: The entire nervous system originates from the neural plate.

questions.question_text: When is the formation of the neural tube completed during gestation?
questions.explanation: The formation of the neural tube is completed by the fourth week of gestation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures include the tectum?
questions.explanation: The tectum is a structure within the mesencephalon (midbrain).

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures differentiate into striatum and pallidum?
questions.explanation: The telencephalon differentiates into structures including the striatum and pallidum.

questions.question_text: Which of the following structures is responsible for origin of cerebellum?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum originates from the rhombencephalon (hindbrain).

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man was diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia. Which of the following histopathological changes is most likely to be seen in his brain?
questions.explanation: Reactive astrocytosis is a histopathological change seen in frontotemporal dementia.

questions.question_text: A 62-year-old man was diagnosed with vascular dementia. Which of the following represents the histopathological changes of his condition?
questions.explanation: Vascular dementia is characterized by histopathological changes including infarction and ischaemia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is classified as both a tauopathy and an amyloidopathy?
questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is classified as both a tauopathy and an amyloidopathy.

questions.question_text: A 72-year-old man was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease according to the criteria of the consortium to establish a registry for Alzheimer's disease (CERAD). Which of the following is not considered a part of the CERAD criteria?
questions.explanation: Prion deposition is not part of the CERAD criteria for Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old man presented with glial nodules, rhabdomyoma of the heart and subungal angiofibroma. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis is characterized by glial nodules, rhabdomyoma of the heart, and subungal angiofibroma.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common cerebral tumour?
questions.explanation: Gliomas are the most common cerebral tumours, derived from glial cells.

questions.question_text: What is the average number of sleep cycles that a person goes through during the night?
questions.explanation: On average, a person goes through 3–5 sleep cycles each night.

questions.question_text: According to the Erlanger and Gasser classification, which of the following nerve fibres have the maximum conduction velocity?
questions.explanation: Aα fibres have the highest conduction velocity among the compared nerve fibres.

questions.question_text: Which of the following receptors is linked with moderate type of transmitter system?
questions.explanation: GABA-B receptors are linked with a moderate type of transmitter system involving second messenger pathways.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a metabotrophic receptor?
questions.explanation: Histamine receptors (H1, H2, H3) are examples of metabotrophic receptors.

questions.question_text: In the membrane transport system, there is a protein that withdraws the vesicle membrane from the synaptic cleft. What is the name of this protein?
questions.explanation: Clathrin is responsible for withdrawing the vesicle membrane from the synaptic cleft.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the action of calmodulin in the transmitter transport system?

options.text: Brings vesicle into contact with the presynaptic membrane
Expels vesicle content into the synaptic cleft
Pinches the neck of the developing vesicles to complete its separation
Withdraws the vesicle membrane from the synaptic cleft

correct_answer.text: Expels vesicle content into the synaptic cleft

correct_answers.text: Expels vesicle content into the synaptic cleft

questions.explanation: Calmodulin is involved in expelling vesicle content into the synaptic cleft.

questions.question_text: Which type of nerve fibre innervates deep pressure sensors in muscles?
questions.explanation: Type III nerve fibres innervate deep pressure sensors in muscles.

questions.question_text: Which type of nerve fibre has a velocity of 25–70 m/s?
questions.explanation: Type II nerve fibres have a conduction velocity of 25–70 m/s.

questions.question_text: Which hormone is secreted by the posterior pituitary?
questions.explanation: The posterior pituitary secretes antidiuretic hormone (ADH).

questions.question_text: Which of the following enzymes converts dopamine to noradrenaline?
questions.explanation: Dopamine β-hydroxylase converts dopamine to noradrenaline.

questions.question_text: Which of the following enzymes is responsible for the degradation of monoamines in presynaptic neuron vesicles?
questions.explanation: Catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) is responsible for degrading monoamines in presynaptic neuron vesicles.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a precursor in the synthesis of noradrenaline?
questions.explanation: l-Tyrosine is a precursor in the synthesis of noradrenaline.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes dopamine?
questions.explanation: Dopamine is synthesised from l-tyrosine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following enzymes is responsible for the degradation of monoamines in the synapse?
questions.explanation: Catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) is responsible for degrading monoamines in the synapse.

questions.question_text: Which enzyme is inhibited by disulfiram?
questions.explanation: Disulfiram inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase.

questions.question_text: Leigh's disease is often characterised by symmetrical necrosis manifested on CT or MRI. What part of the brain is involved in this process?
questions.explanation: Leigh's disease involves the basal ganglia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following imaging technique involves use of radioactive compounds to study regional differences in blood flow in the brain?
questions.explanation: Single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) uses radioactive compounds to study blood flow.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old man was diagnosed with dementia with Lewy bodies. Which of the following findings is likely to be observed on SPECT?

options.text: Reduced blood flow in frontal lobe
Reduced blood flow in parietal lobe
Reduced blood flow in temporal lobes
Reduced blood flow in occipital lobe
Variable and multifocal areas of reduced blood flow

correct_answer.text: Reduced blood flow in occipital lobe

correct_answers.text: Reduced blood flow in occipital lobe

questions.explanation: Dementia with Lewy bodies shows reduced blood flow in the occipital lobe on SPECT.

questions.question_text: Which of the following changes is seen on neuroimaging in patients with schizophrenia?

options.text: Increased activity in the frontal lobe
Reduced phospholipids in the frontal lobe

correct_answer.text: Reduced phospholipids in the frontal lobe

correct_answers.text: Reduced phospholipids in the frontal lobe

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia patients show reduced phospholipids in the frontal lobe on neuroimaging.

questions.question_text: A medical student wanted to know what was used in MRI to construct images of tissues. What would you tell him?
questions.explanation: Protons, particularly hydrogen nuclei, are used in MRI to construct tissue images.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for antidepressant-induced hyponatremia?
questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus is a risk factor for antidepressant-induced hyponatremia.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old male student of Asian ethnicity drank alcohol for the first time in his life. As soon as he had a glass of beer he developed tachycardia, facial flushing, sweating, and muscle weakness. What is the most likely reason?
questions.explanation: Aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 deficiency is common in Asian populations and causes unpleasant reactions to alcohol.

questions.question_text: A 44-year-old man diagnosed with bipolar affective disorder has recently started taking lithium carbonate 200 mg twice a day. Which of the following blood tests will give a good indication of serum lithium levels?

options.text: A blood test done 12 hours after the last night dose on day 2 of starting lithium carbonate
A blood test done 12 hours after the last night dose on day 10 of starting lithium carbonate and delaying the morning dose till the blood test is done
A blood test done 13 hours after the last night dose on day 10 of starting lithium carbonate while administering the morning dose on time
A blood test done 15 hours after the last night dose on day 10 of starting lithium carbonate while administering the morning dose on time
A blood test done 9 hours after the last night dose on day 10 of starting lithium carbonate while administering the morning dose on time

correct_answer.text: A blood test done 13 hours after the last night dose on day 10 of starting lithium carbonate while administering the morning dose on time

correct_answers.text: A blood test done 13 hours after the last night dose on day 10 of starting lithium carbonate while administering the morning dose on time

questions.explanation: A blood test done 13 hours after the last dose on day 10 provides a good indication of serum lithium levels.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old man has achieved complete remission of depressive illness on treatment with paroxetine. He stopped taking paroxetine abruptly without seeking medical advice and experienced tremors, sweating and electric shock-like sensations in his legs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Abrupt stopping of paroxetine can lead to discontinuation syndrome, characterized by tremors, sweating, and electric shock-like sensations.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old woman has recurrent depressive disorder on fluoxetine 60 mg with limited benefit. You had a discussion with the patient to stop fluoxetine and start mirtazapine. According to NICE guidelines, which of the following is the most appropriate way to do it?

options.text: Reduce fluoxetine to 40 mg and start mirtazapine 15 mg
Reduce fluoxetine to 20 mg and start mirtazapine 15 mg
Stop fluoxetine, wait for 4–7 days and start mirtazapine

questions.explanation: NICE guidelines recommend a cautious cross-tapering of fluoxetine with mirtazapine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about treatment during breastfeeding is correct?

options.text: Diazepam is preferred over lorazepam for anxiety
Fluoxetine is the preferred antidepressant drug
Lamotrigine is preferred for bipolar depression
Lithium is preferred as a mood stabiliser
Olanzapine is the preferred antipsychotic drug

correct_answer.text: Olanzapine is the preferred antipsychotic drug

correct_answers.text: Olanzapine is the preferred antipsychotic drug

questions.explanation: Olanzapine is preferred as an antipsychotic drug during breastfeeding.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the implications of COMT genetics is correct?

options.text: Met genotype of COMT increases the risk of problems with cognitive performance
Met genotype of COMT predisposes to the risk of schizophrenia
People with Met genotype of COMT have higher dopamine levels
Val genotype of COMT increases the reactivity to life stressors
Val genotype of COMT predisposes to the risk of anxiety disorders

correct_answer.text: People with Met genotype of COMT have higher dopamine levels

correct_answers.text: People with Met genotype of COMT have higher dopamine levels

questions.explanation: Individuals with the Met genotype of COMT have lower enzyme activity, resulting in higher dopamine levels.

questions.question_text: A 68-year-old man diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease was started on memantine. He reported sudden worsening of cognitive symptoms 3 weeks after starting the treatment. What is the most likely reason for this?
questions.explanation: Memantine's antagonism of nicotine acetylcholine receptors can worsen cognitive symptoms.

questions.question_text: Administration of clonidine stimulates growth hormone release. What is the mechanism of action?
questions.explanation: Clonidine acts as an α2-adrenoreceptor agonist, stimulating growth hormone release.

questions.question_text: A 48-year-old man presented to the accident and emergency department with complaints of inner restlessness, agitation and an inability to sit. He has been taking fluoxetine for the past week for depression. What is the most likely cause for these symptoms?

options.text: Blockade of cholinergic receptors in the striatum
Direct dopamine receptor agonism in the striatum
Direct dopamine receptor blockade at the striatum
Indirectly stimulating 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT2A) receptors which results in excess of dopamine release
Indirectly stimulating 5-HT2A receptors which results in inhibition of dopamine release

correct_answer.text: Indirectly stimulating 5-HT2A receptors which results in inhibition of dopamine release

correct_answers.text: Indirectly stimulating 5-HT2A receptors which results in inhibition of dopamine release

questions.explanation: Fluoxetine can indirectly stimulate 5-HT2A receptors, leading to inhibition of dopamine release, causing akathisia.

questions.question_text: Ketamine can produce symptoms that are similar to those in schizophrenia. What is the likely mechanism involved?
questions.explanation: Ketamine blocks NMDA receptors, which can produce schizophrenia-like symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about acamprosate is correct?

options.text: It is a derivative of the amino acid valine
Its main site of action is the ventral tegmental area

correct_answer.text: Its main site of action is the ventral tegmental area

correct_answers.text: Its main site of action is the ventral tegmental area

questions.explanation: Acamprosate acts primarily in the ventral tegmental area to modulate glutamate and GABA neurotransmission.

questions.question_text: If the frequency of the depot antipsychotic injection is every 2 weeks, then how many milligrams of zuclopenthixol decanoate would be approximately equivalent to 40 milligrams of flupenthixol decanoate?
questions.explanation: According to Table 3.2, 40 mg of flupenthixol decanoate every 2 weeks is approximately equivalent to 200 mg of zuclopenthixol decanoate every 2 weeks.

questions.question_text: A 42-year-old woman presented with symptoms of stress incontinence. Your consultant asked you to start her on an antidepressant medication. Which of the following would you consider?
questions.explanation: Duloxetine is indicated for both the treatment of depression and stress urinary incontinence by inhibiting the reuptake of serotonin and noradrenaline.

questions.question_text: You have discussed the concept of potency of medication in your teachings with medical students. Which of the following selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors is the most potent?
questions.explanation: Paroxetine is the most potent selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) among those listed.

questions.question_text: A 46-year-old man with schizophrenia presented to the outpatient clinic with 'fly-catching tongue'. What is the most likely cause of this sign?
questions.explanation: 'Fly-catching tongue' is a sign of tardive dyskinesia, a movement disorder associated with long-term use of antipsychotic medications.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely due to concomitant use of sodium valproate and lamotrigine?

options.text: Lamotrigine levels decrease due to induction of glucuronidation by sodium valproate
Lamotrigine levels increase due to inhibition of glucuronidation by sodium valproate
There is no effect on lamotrigine levels
Sodium valproate levels increase due to inhibition of glucuronidation by lamotrigine
Sodium valproate levels increase due to induction of glucuronidation by lamotrigine

correct_answer.text: Lamotrigine levels increase due to inhibition of glucuronidation by sodium valproate

correct_answers.text: Lamotrigine levels increase due to inhibition of glucuronidation by sodium valproate

questions.explanation: Sodium valproate inhibits glucuronidation, leading to increased levels of lamotrigine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is least likely to precipitate closed-angle glaucoma?
questions.explanation: Lithium is not typically associated with precipitating closed-angle glaucoma, unlike the other listed drugs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is least likely to cause sexual dysfunction?
questions.explanation: Bupropion is less likely to cause sexual dysfunction compared to other antidepressants listed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants is recommended in patients who had antidepressant-induced hyperprolactinaemia?
questions.explanation: Mirtazapine is recommended as it is less likely to cause hyperprolactinaemia.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman with a diagnosis of bipolar affective disorder had four episodes of depression in the past decade and one hypomanic episode 15 years ago. Which of the following drugs is most appropriate as a prophylactic treatment?
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine is effective in preventing depressive episodes in bipolar affective disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line antipsychotic to treat psychosis in Parkinson's disease?
questions.explanation: Quetiapine is preferred due to its better tolerability and lower risk of exacerbating Parkinson's symptoms.

questions.question_text: You have reviewed a 24-year-old man who has misused multiple substances and presented with psychotic symptoms. He was started on quetiapine. He was later prescribed a drug by the substance misuse service after confirmation that he was abstinent from drugs except heroin. Unfortunately, the patient, on taking the drug, collapsed and died. Which of the following is the most likely drug to have been used?
questions.explanation: Methadone can prolong the QTc interval, especially when combined with antipsychotics like quetiapine, increasing the risk of fatal arrhythmias.

questions.question_text: In alcohol dependence, disulfiram is used for aversion therapy. What is its mechanism of action?

options.text: It is an alcohol dehydrogenase inhibitor
It is an aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor
It is a γ-aminobutyric acid A (GABA-A) agonist

correct_answer.text: It is an aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor

correct_answers.text: It is an aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor

questions.explanation: Disulfiram inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, leading to acetaldehyde accumulation when alcohol is consumed, causing unpleasant symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is most accurate about novel treatment approaches being studied for schizophrenia?

options.text: Memantine and amantadine are hypothesised to be an option to treat schizophrenia
Metabotrophic postsynaptic glutamate receptors agonists have shown improvements in symptoms of schizophrenia
NMDA antagonists can improve the positive, cognitive and negative symptoms of schizophrenia
NMDA antagonists improve neurons in schizophrenia, so they could be helpful, particularly early in the disease process
NMDA receptors are hyperfunctional in schizophrenia, so glutamate agonists are hypothesised to be helpful to treat it

correct_answer.text: Metabotrophic postsynaptic glutamate receptors agonists have shown improvements in symptoms of schizophrenia

correct_answers.text: Metabotrophic postsynaptic glutamate receptors agonists have shown improvements in symptoms of schizophrenia

questions.explanation: Metabotrophic postsynaptic glutamate receptors agonists have shown improvements in schizophrenia symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is most accurate about the novel experimental treatment options for schizophrenia?

options.text: d-Cycloserine, a glycine antagonist, has shown some promise for treating schizophrenia
Glycine transporters/GlyT1 pump inhibitors increase synaptic availability of glycine, and thus reduce NMDA transmission to improve schizophrenia symptoms
LY404039 can reverse phencyclidine (PCP)-induced behavioural changes in animals
Sarcosine is a naturally occurring glycine antagonist that has been shown to improve schizophrenia symptoms
Some amount of dopamine receptor blockade is essential to treat the symptoms of schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: LY404039 can reverse phencyclidine (PCP)-induced behavioural changes in animals

correct_answers.text: LY404039 can reverse phencyclidine (PCP)-induced behavioural changes in animals

questions.explanation: LY404039, a selective mGluR2/3 agonist, can reverse PCP-induced behavioral changes in animal models of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: In mitotic cell division, which of the following stages of cell division does not involve repetition?
questions.explanation: Interphase is the phase of the cell cycle that does not involve repetition of the division stages.

questions.question_text: 'Knock out' is a technique used in genetics. What is the purpose of this technique?
questions.explanation: 'Knock out' techniques are used for functional analysis by inactivating specific genes to study their functions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is consistent with the RNA-splicing enzyme?

options.text: Excises large portions of mRNA during transcription
Excises large portions of rRNA during transcription
Excises large portions of tRNA during transcription
Excises large portions of tRNA during translation
Modifies the ends of the RNA molecule

correct_answer.text: Excises large portions of tRNA during transcription

correct_answers.text: Excises large portions of tRNA during transcription

questions.explanation: RNA-splicing enzymes excise large portions of tRNA during transcription.

questions.question_text: What is a possible mechanism to bring about persistent genetic change in response to environmental stressors?
questions.explanation: Chromatin remodelling is an epigenetic mechanism that can lead to persistent genetic changes in response to environmental factors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has DNA methylation as a critical step?
questions.explanation: DNA methylation is a critical step in genomic imprinting, an epigenetic process.

questions.question_text: The chromatids of the homologous chromosome in the metaphase of meiosis exchange segments by breakage. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Synapsis is the pairing of homologous chromosomes during meiosis where recombination occurs.

questions.question_text: On which of the following is chromosomal analysis usually carried out?
questions.explanation: Chromosomal analysis is typically performed on white blood cells as they are readily accessible and proliferate in culture.

questions.question_text: What is aneuploidy?

options.text: Alteration in the number of sex chromosomes
Alteration in the number of autosomes
Alteration in the number of sex chromosomes or autosomes
Description of the fragile site on a chromosome
Gain of an extra segment of chromosome

correct_answer.text: Alteration in the number of sex chromosomes or autosomes

correct_answers.text: Alteration in the number of sex chromosomes or autosomes

questions.explanation: Aneuploidy refers to an abnormal number of chromosomes, either sex chromosomes or autosomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following about robertsonian translocation is correct?

options.text: Exchange of segment between two different pairs of chromosomes
Fusion of two chromosomes at their centromere
Translocation of a segment of one chromosome on a fragile site to another chromosome
When segment of a chromosome included twice over
When segment of chromosome detached and then reattached in opposite orientation

correct_answer.text: Fusion of two chromosomes at their centromere

correct_answers.text: Fusion of two chromosomes at their centromere

questions.explanation: Robertsonian translocation involves the fusion of two acrocentric chromosomes at their centromeres.

questions.question_text: Which of the following shows anticipation?
questions.explanation: Anticipation is seen in disorders caused by dynamic mutations, such as trinucleotide repeat expansions.

questions.question_text: What defect is seen in disorders of 'imprinting' such as Prader–Willi syndrome and Angelman's syndrome?
questions.explanation: DNA methylation is a critical defect seen in imprinting disorders like Prader–Willi and Angelman's syndromes.

questions.question_text: What does the term 'horizontal inheritance' in genetics mean?

options.text: Transmission of disease from mother to child
Transmission of disease from father to child
The phenomenon in which affected individuals are found in every generation
The phenomenon in which affected individuals are seen every second generation
No case occurring in previous generation, but the disease manifesting in children of next generation

correct_answer.text: No case occurring in previous generation, but the disease manifesting in children of next generation

correct_answers.text: No case occurring in previous generation, but the disease manifesting in children of next generation

questions.explanation: Horizontal inheritance refers to situations where no cases occurred in previous generations, but the disease manifests in the children of the next generation.

questions.question_text: Gene mapping helps to locate and identify genes in psychiatric disorders. What is the most widely used genetic marker for gene mapping?
questions.explanation: Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are the most widely used genetic markers for gene mapping.

questions.question_text: The fact that 'high levels of licking and grooming in early life of rat pups by mothers alter brain glucocorticoid expression and stress sensitivity in offspring' is an example of gene regulation. Which of the following is involved in this process?
questions.explanation: Environmental factors acting through biological mechanisms, such as maternal care, can regulate gene expression.

questions.question_text: What do we call the study of diseases in families when co-segregation of the disease and a set of genetic markers are investigated?
questions.explanation: Genetic linkage refers to the co-segregation of disease with genetic markers within families.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the recombinant fraction is correct?

options.text: It is the most important parameter involved in gene mapping
It is the proportion of cross-over that occurs in metaphase of mitosis
It is the total number of recombinants multiplied by number of off-springs
It is zero when the two loci are very close together

correct_answer.text: It is zero when the two loci are very close together

correct_answers.text: It is zero when the two loci are very close together

questions.explanation: The recombinant fraction is zero when two loci are very close together on a chromosome.

questions.question_text: In linkage analysis, what logarithm of the odd (LOD) score is accepted by convention to signify the linkage that has been detected?
questions.explanation: A LOD score of 3 or higher is conventionally accepted as evidence of linkage.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?

options.text: Genetic variation in a population will remain constant from one generation to the next in the absence of disturbing factors
In a population, both genotype and allelic frequencies keep changing
The phenotype and allelic frequencies in a population are not in equilibrium
There is a continuous change of phenotypes in a population from one generation to the next
There is a continuous change of genes in a population from one generation to the next

correct_answer.text: Genetic variation in a population will remain constant from one generation to the next in the absence of disturbing factors

correct_answers.text: Genetic variation in a population will remain constant from one generation to the next in the absence of disturbing factors

questions.explanation: Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium states that genetic variation remains constant across generations without disturbing factors.

questions.question_text: A 38-year-old white man migrated to the USA and started a new relationship with an Asian woman. They have two children. How are the genetic changes that occur in his children best described?
questions.explanation: Gene flow involves the transfer of genetic variation from one population to another, as seen in this interracial relationship.

questions.question_text: To which of the following genes is P50 suppression linked?
questions.explanation: P50 suppression is linked to the nicotinic receptor gene, specifically the α7-subunit.

questions.question_text: You are assessing a 14-year-old boy with a family history suggestive of both parents having schizophrenia. What are the chances of this boy developing schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: There is approximately a 50% chance of developing schizophrenia if both parents have the disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about twin studies in schizophrenia is correct?

options.text: Dizygotic (DZ) probandwise concordance rate is around 24%
More than four-fifths of the variance in causes of schizophrenia are genetically determined
Monozygotic (MZ) probandwise concordance rate is around 66%
Probandwise concordance rate is defined as the percentage of probands who have an affected sibling whether or not a twin
Probandwise concordance rates are the same using the ICD-10 and DSM-IV criteria

correct_answer.text: More than four-fifths of the variance in causes of schizophrenia are genetically determined

correct_answers.text: More than four-fifths of the variance in causes of schizophrenia are genetically determined

questions.explanation: More than four-fifths of the variance in the causes of schizophrenia are genetically determined.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about genetics in eating disorders is correct?

options.text: Among female siblings of patients with established anorexia nervosa (AN), 5–10% of them have the condition compared with 0.5–1.0% found in the general population of the same age
Concordance rate for AN in DZ twins is 15%
Concordance rate for AN in MZ twins is 40%
Inherited liability to AN does not involve relevant personality traits such as perfectionism and obsessionality
There is no association between eating disorders and mood disorders

correct_answer.text: Among female siblings of patients with established anorexia nervosa (AN), 5–10% of them have the condition compared with 0.5–1.0% found in the general population of the same age

correct_answers.text: Among female siblings of patients with established anorexia nervosa (AN), 5–10% of them have the condition compared with 0.5–1.0% found in the general population of the same age

questions.explanation: Female siblings of patients with AN have a higher prevalence (5–10%) compared to the general population (0.5–1.0%).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about family and twin studies in unipolar depression and bipolar affective disorder is correct?

options.text: In unipolar depression, the concordance rate is 46% in MZ and 20% in DZ twins
Overall, the genetic influence in bipolar affective disorder is less than in unipolar depression
Relatives of bipolar probands have an increased risk of schizoaffective disorder and bipolar affective disorder, but not unipolar depression
Relatives of patients with unipolar depression have an increased risk of bipolar or schizoaffective disorder
The concordance rate for mood disorders in the MZ co-twin of a proband with bipolar affective disorder is between 60 and 70%, and for DZ twins the rate is about 40%
